neighbours.label: ' of' linking an abstract or collective noun to what it belongs to ('the good of his nation', 'the things of this world')
fire: She said that real peace comes when you stop chasing the pleasures of this world and look inward.
He promised to use his wealth for the welfare of his people rather than for himself.
The pastor spoke about the children of God gathered in the small chapel that night.
Many economists have written about the cost of inequality in modern democracies.
They were sent to serve the poor of the city during the long winter famine.
The novel describes the glory of the empire at the height of its power.
Every generation must decide what it owes to the future of its country and its children.
The bishop prayed for the souls of the departed in the crowded cathedral.
